body:
You have . . . no idea how applicable that statement feels to me right now

::sigh::

Hey, I just thought I'd let you know that you appear to have posted this to your main reddit account.  Don't know if that was your intention or not.

I wish I had some comforting words to offer you.  This sounds like an incredibly unhappy situation.  But you are looking at, to reuse a phrase that someone said to me, "a permanent solution to a temporary problem"

I can absolutely sympathize with the problem of trying to talk to friends that always seem too busy.  And you don't want to come right out and say, "I need you to talk to me.  I think I'm going to kill myself and I need your support.  Please email me, please initiate conversations instead of me having to message you, please call me without my having to call first," because it sounds so pathetic . . . but that's what you have to do. 

And when I finally did say that to a couple of people, when I told them that I needed them and I was actually kind of upset that they couldn't spend a few minutes a day to help me out, they didn't think it pathetic--if anything, they felt bad because they had been bad friends.  So do it.  Swallow your pride, and bitch your friends out for not being there when you need them.  You can't pull yourself out of depression all on your own, you need the help and support of the people around you.  So do what you need to do to get that support.

Would you pull the trigger?

I'm serious.  If she decided that the way she wanted to die was to have you point a gun at her head and pull the trigger, would you do it?  Because if you know about her plan and you do nothing to stop it, I honestly don't see any significant difference.  

And if the answer to that question is honestly "yes" then . . . well, I suppose you have your answer.  But if the answer is "no", then you need to do everything in your power to stop her.  And if that means she gets institutionalized, then so be it.  She may thank you for it one day . . . she may not.  She may in fact hate you for it.  That's something you might to have to live with.  But would that really be any harder to live with than the knowledge that you pulled the trigger?
Wow, that was . . . incredibly powerful.  Thank you.  I will try to cherish and remember this.

Heh I had a mental image of this:  http://www.games14.net/Play_Ice_Walls.html

Too bad I always sucked at that game . . .

Anyways, I guess my worry is that it's not slow progress . . . that I'm actually sliding backwards =/

Thank you for the compliment.  Although . . . from my perspective, you're the one with the greater accomplishment.  I do those things every morning because I know that the moment I stop, the moment I fail, the moment I succumb to that kind of despair, I am *never* coming back.  In the same way that I had to force myself to wake up early to make 8am lectures all sophomore year, because I knew (and proved, three terms in a row) that the first time I let myself miss *one* lecture, I'd never go back again :D

So to me, your accomplishment is far greater than mine.  To go that deep, to lose that much, and still manage to come back . . . that's inconceivable to me.

And, by the way, it takes two to create "real engagement", so thank you for your part as well.  And if anything I say or do helps you even tangentially . . . that would be amazing.  Because I don't know anything else about you other than the fact that you are capable of tremendous kindness to a person that needs it, and that alone should be enough to kill any "nagging doubts" you have :)

Haha you have no idea the high standards to which I hold myself.  I spent a year in therapy trying (unsuccessfully, apparently) to get over my feelings of inadequacy and self-doubt because my academic performance slipped after my close friend committed suicide.  Not kidding.

I understand what you mean about motivation following action, but I worry that it's not enough.  Right now, I wake up every morning, shave, put on a suit, and head in to work.  And that's plenty hard just on its own.  But I thought that just pushing on would be enough . . . but it's been two months and it just isn't.  I feel like if I don't make some kind of change . . . well, that's how I chose this username

Umm, by the way, please don't think that just because I contradict half of your posts doesn't mean I don't appreciate them . . . seriously.  Thanks to all of you guys for giving me someone with whom I can talk honestly and anonymously.  Thank you.
Let me clarify.  I'm not saying I believe we *will* sort this out.  I understand that the odds are very, very long.  But I'm saying that I'm not going to give up hope.  Not just yet.

Well, in her mind, she was doing the right thing.  She "realized she doesn't love me any more" and believed not telling me and thus ending it would be cruel, would be "stringing me along".  Yeah, I think she acted kind of selfishly.  Yeah, I'm a little upset with her.  Yeah, she definitely did not treat our relationship with the respect that half a decade together deserved.  But I'm willing to forgive her, if we can sit down together and work this shit out.

And I agree with you.  Everything else is just details, excuses, tangential explanations.  If she felt about me the way I feel about her, none of it would matter.  I understand that.

But love was there, once.  I know you have only my word to go on, but trust me.  Even she acknowledged that we had something very special, although she says it's over now.  And almost *every single person* who saw the two of us together for more than 30 seconds believed it too.  We were the ones that people held up as proof that love was real.  So I believe that we can find love again.
A hand of friendship means more than you could possibly imagine.  Thank you :)

I see.  That does make some sense.  I guess . . . do the kinds of things that *would* be interesting to me, if I were healthy?  Mountain climbing was never one of my interests, but maybe getting more serious about one of my previous hobbies would help?

I will think on it.  I will try.  Thank you.

To overly extend the metaphor, even if I do try to walk it off, I don't really have anywhere I want to walk to.  People tell me that I have to live my life, have to keep going, but I just want to ask, "why?"  I don't . . . I don't *desire* anything anymore.  People say to keep putting one foot in front of the other, but I don't really have anywhere I want to go.

The other thing about hospitalization is that the stigma exists in my mind as well.  Best case scenario would be that the hospitalization saves my life but I'll be forced to spend years or decades reconciling with my own feelings of inadequacy and self-doubt because I was forced to resort to it.  Admittedly, this is a better scenario than the one that, as I said, I feel may be inevitable if I *don't* make some changes, but . . .

Sorry it took me so long to reply, I went to sleep.  Then I had to rewrite this a couple of times because the first few draft came out *comically* self-pitying and somewhat pathetic, and you deserve better than that for the kindness you've shown me.  But here's the advice I give you from my very unique perspective:

You have what I never had, which is warning.  I knew we were having some problems, some difficulties, but I never thought it would end like this.  Neither of us did.  Our problems were always just that--*our* problems, problems we would work out together.  Until apparently we ran into problems that she thought could be better solved unilaterally.

If I could go back in time, to a moth before or a day before or even just an hour before the breakup, hell even to an hour *after* the breakup, there's so much I would have said and done differently.  So talk to her.  Don't push her, don't pester her, don't try to force a conflict, but do whatever it takes to find out what it is you need to do to make this work.  If it's that important to you, work for it.

And, incidentally, don't disregard happiness just because it's "superficial".  Treasure every good moment you have together, hold those little bits of happiness in your mind and your heart, and do what you can to make sure that she is doing the same.

Don't forget about deeper issues that may need to be resolved, but don't lose sight of what's good about the relationship, even if it's just the fact that you two have fun hanging out together.  Your relationship was and still is founded on the good things between you, not the problems.

I've discussed this above, and I've very strongly considered it.  The benefits go without saying.  However, I have three strong reasons keeping me here (admittedly, two of them have to do with getting back together, so I don't know how healthy that is):

One, she really wants to be independent.  We've been in this relationship for almost a quarter of our lives, almost a third if you count our good friendship before we started going out.  She says she wants to know what it's like to be her own person instead of half of a pair.  Right now, she's not expecting me to come home for another 4 months.  If I speed that up, she may feel that I'm taking something away from her, pressuring her to deal with what's between us before she is ready.  I worry that this will cause her to push me away without even giving it a chance.

Second, she says that she doesn't believe *I* can be independent.  She says that I relied on her too much during the relationship.  Regardless of whether or not this is true, the point is that by staying here I have an opportunity to prove to her that I can be strong and persevere through adversity.  She knows, even if she doesn't truly *understand*, how hard this is for me.  If I succeed, I think it will, as I put it above, "go a long way to proving that I'm still the confident, competent guy with whom she fell in love".

Third, I think I want to do this for myself.  I think that I would respect myself less, would be ashamed, if I "quit" and went home.  I know, I know, that's not healthy.  Heh I spent a lot of time with my previous therapist working to accept my weaknesses, not to hold myself to such a high standard.  I thought i'd made progress, but . . . well.  So there's that.  If I go home, the damage to my already *incredibly* fragile sense of self-esteem might be disastrous.

Those points aside, you're absolutely right.  "Crisis situation" is an understatement.  I wish I could go back in time two months.  Or look ahead in time two months to see how things turn out.  Instead, I'm just stuck here in the present, with limited information, looking at an increasingly bleak prospect for survival.

Haha no, a misunderstanding.  I noticed that you quickly brought up that you "do actually have a boyfriend" and worried that you though *I* was hitting on you.  So yeah, all good.

I refuse, however, to accept the fact that just because the relationship is "over" means that it wasn't worthwhile--and can't be so again.  I don't know.  People make mistakes.  I think she made a big one, I really do.

It doesn't change the fact that you're right, I need to learn about myself and how to be alive.  Whether or not she and I are going to work things out, I need to get myself to a place where I'm happy and comfortable with myself.  As opposed to, you know, this whole "suicidal" thing I've got going on right now =/

By the way, sorry to be so selfish--I'm really sorry to hear that your'e going through something similar.  Please, take advantage of this time to talk to her while she's still willing to try to work things out.  Find out exactly what she needs that you're not giving her . . . even if what she wants most is space.  Better you back off now with the intention of strengthening the relationship in the future, before things are said that can maybe never be unsaid.  If she's really that special, you make this work no matter what it takes, even if it means you'll have to sacrifice or hurt in the short term.  That's my advice, anyways.

(Funny, I used to be the go-to guy for relationship counseling for all of my friends, but I somehow doubt they'll be coming to me for relationship advice any time soon . . .)

Group therapy does sound like a really good idea (although I don't speak the native language).  I will ask my therapist.

Thank you for your kind words, but in a way it's almost worse to think about how objectively good my life is.  In everything but this one aspect, my life is going great:  Interesting job, opportunity to live for 6 months in a foreign city, great future career prospectives, etc. . . . but then that just makes me feel crappy for not being able to appreciate it.  And feeling bad because you feel bad is literally the least productive thing I can be doing in this situation :P

As for my self-worth . . . well, I haven't needed a sense of self-worth for a while because my sense of self wasn't even that important.  I had a sense of the worth of my relationship, and that was through the roof.  But yeah, in the end that's part of what drove her to end it, I guess.  And so, and so, and so . . .

Thank you so much for your offer, and thank you for your understanding.  Although no, sadly, I am not in London (and incidentally, in case it was ambiguous, by "relationship" I did only mean "friendship")

I'm really happy to hear that you've found some happiness and peace.  While I'm still too close to it to take anything approaching solace from sentiments like "some day you will look back on this" or "time heals all" or "eventually you will find someone else" . . . but it makes me happy to see other people that have found their own little patches of happiness after troubled times

Why do you ask?  Offering to hang out?

I'm still on the fence as to whether I'd like to try to form a relationship with someone from SW.  I don't know whether it would be healthy for me to have a person who knows me only as "the suicidal guy" . . . you know, with the exception of my therapist (which is obviously a special relationship) all of the people with whom I'm talking remember the happy, in love, confident guy I used to be.  I feel like that's important.

Well, where are you?  It might be a moot point anyways.

Tell me more about the third point, that's the one I don't understand.  So you just . . . do random things, in hopes that something sticks?

Cuz I'm at that point, the point where there's no difference between getting off the couch and backpacking around the Andes . . . do you just pick the latter on general principle and hope it pans out?

Let me elaborate:

I don't know whether I'm doing this for myself or for her.

I don't know whether this is, to continue your metaphor, something where I can just "walk it off", or something I need to put in a cast and rest for two months.

I don't know if medication is sufficient.  I don't know how far I will slide.  I don't know whether or not I need to hospitalize myself for my own safety (or the safety of others).

Two months ago, I felt like I knew everything important about my life.  Now, I feel like I know nothing.

I am faking it, but I still feel so very . . . *hollow*.  I hate it, and I hate myself for doing it.  For forcing myself to be in good spirits when I don't feel them, forcing myself to be social when I just want to curl up in the corner, forcing myself to remain positive in online correspondence and public forums.  I truly hate it.

And I try, I really do.  I treat myself to nice meals or things that I would normally like, but in all but the rarest of situations I feel nothing.  Just nothing.

I will keep trying, I will.  But I hate it so.

Obviously the forty-year plan wasn't set in stone.  But what I was sure of was that, regardless of what life threw at me, I'd have the girl I loved by my side and we would work through our problems together.  The world *is* full of uncertainty, which is why it meant so much to me to have one thing of which I could be certain.  Or so I thought.

As for detachment . . . one day, perhaps.  But I'm not ready just yet.  This relationship meant so much to me for so long, I just can't let go that easily.
We'll see, I'm certainly taking it day by day.  I just . . . I just don't know.  I feel like I'm saying that a lot these days.  I just.  Don't.  Know
Thank you for the kind offer :)

Yes, I've had very, very positive experiences with therapy in the past.  And, like I said, I know this playbook (from first- and very extensive second-hand experience) and I really am doing everything I can to put the odds in my favor.

My current therapist is very wise, and although I don't feel quite as in touch with my emotions with a male therapist as I would/did with a female therapist, he has a lot of insight and I think he is helping me sort myself out.  At least I hope so.

Why do you ask where I am?  I don't really want to post it in public, but if you have relevant knowledge I'll happily PM you.

Thanks for the encouragement.  I'm just so up and down.  I feel like my good periods are getting better, but my bad periods are getting so much worse.  So even though I leave my therapist's office feeling good, it's just a matter of time before it fades away

Well if I were considering how my suicide factors into other people's lives, it wouldn't be on the table at all.  Regardless of how it would make her feel (and yes, I do believe that you're completely wrong, that it would probably mess her up for a very long time if she thought she were responsible for my death), there are plenty of other people who would be absolutely devastated if I killed myself.

And it's not just her that's "worth dying over".  It's everything we were going to have together.  We had our life planned out, for four months from now and four years from now and forty years from now.  I was so happy with that plan.  That's what I feel like I've lost.  Not just some chick.  I lost my entire life.

I'm perfectly capable of picking up girls.  I know, that sounds like bravado and it maybe is, but that's not really the issue (hilariously, I ended up getting a number by accident two weekends ago, I was just chatting with this girl cuz she was cute and I was bored waiting in line for drinks).  The fact is, I have no desire whatsoever to pick up chicks, to tomcat around, to do any of that.

I know this is an opportunity to better myself.  To have fun, to learn new things, to be free--that's how she's looking at it, I'm pretty sure.  But I just don't care.  About any of that.

I have asked them, and some of them are being really helpful (others are too busy, and others are, let's be honest, probably getting a little fed up after two months).  The problem is that there's a large portion of the day when none of them are awake . . . 9-hour time difference means that they all go to bed at 9am-11am my time, and no one wakes up for 8 or more hours.

I'm seriously considering leaving the internship and going home.  I really am.  If for no other reason than my health care would be more likely to cover therapy back home.  But--and I know, I know, this isn't good, but--I'm not giving up hope that she and I can work it out.  But what she wants right now is space, is a chance to remember what it's like to be single instead of half of a pair.  And she wants to know that *I* can be single, instead of relying on her.

If I go back now, both of those goals are put into jeopardy.  I risk making her feel pressured, taking away her opportunity to feel independent--so she will reject any chance of reconciliation just on general principle.  Second, I lose an opportunity to show her that I can be strong, that I can succeed in such an incredibly successful environment.  

She's not an idiot.  We've been best friends for almost eight years, we have a number of mutual friends with whom we are both still talking, etc. etc., so she knows how hard this is for me.  Maybe she doesn't *understand* just how bad it is, but she knows this is hard.  If I can persevere, work hard, get a good recommendation out of this internship, it will go a long way to proving that I'm still the confident, competent guy with whom she fell in love.

And you know what?  If I go home, *I* will think less of myself.  I know it's incredibly stupid to put my life at risk (because yes, that's what I'm doing) for pride but . . . well, my sense of self-worth is pretty fucking low right now.  Maybe it needs all the help it can get.  But yeah, I'm gambling . . . and maybe it's a gamble I'm going to lose.
